title: Post-selected enhancement of phase sensitivity in a two-path interferometer
authors: Ryuya Fukuda, Katsuki Tanaka, Masataka Iinuma, Holger F. Hofmann
abstract: Post-selected metrology can exceed the standard quantum limit of single photon interference by concentrating all of the available Fisher information in a subset of post-selected outcomes. Here we apply this principle to a standard two-path interferometer, activating the Fisher information concentrated in the low probability output port by transferring the phase sensitivity to the circular polarizations of the photon. We obtain a phase gradient of the post-selected interference fringe that corresponds to that of a four-photon NOON state, providing a direct comparison of the performance of multi-photon interference with single-photon post-selection.
summary: This paper demonstrates that by employing post-selection on a two-path interferometer, the phase sensitivity can be significantly enhanced beyond the standard quantum limit. This enhancement is achieved by engineering the input state to entangle path and polarization, effectively mimicking the scaling of a four-photon NOON state. This shows a powerful way to access high-precision quantum metrology using single-photon resources.
main_problem: To enhance the phase sensitivity of a two-path interferometer beyond the standard quantum limit (SQL) using post-selection techniques.
main_result: The achieved phase gradient approaches that of a four-photon NOON state, demonstrating that single-photon interference can reach multi-photon entanglement scaling through post-selection.
method: The enhancement is achieved by preparing an entangled state in the path and polarization degrees of freedom and post-selecting on a low-probability output port.
model_or_system: The system is a conventional two-path interferometer, extended to include polarization states. The phase shift is governed by a path difference operator, and the enhancement relies on transferring phase information to the circular polarization degree of freedom.
key_observables: The conditional probability $P(R|-angle)$ and its derivative (slope) with respect to the phase shift $\phi$.
important_parameters: The effective photon number difference $A_{eff}$, which quantifies the enhancement; the standard quantum limit (SQL).
main_assumptions: The enhancement relies on introducing a slight entanglement between polarization and paths, and the method is limited by experimental imperfections.
figures_summary: Figure 1 schematically shows the setup using HWP1 and HWP2 for polarization rotation. Figure 2 illustrates the measured conditional probability $P(R|-angle)$ vs. $\phi$, showing the enhanced slope near $\phi=0$.
paper_structure: The paper details the theoretical framework for post-selection Fisher information, applies this to the two-path interferometer by incorporating polarization, and presents experimental measurements comparing the measured slope to the theoretical NOON state prediction.
why_interesting: This work provides a concrete experimental demonstration of how measurement selection (post-selection) can effectively simulate the resource scaling of multi-photon entangled states (like NOON states) using only single photons in a standard setup.
